resources.string: %1$d BPM. Enter tempo or swipe vertically
Numerator: 1–1024 · Denominator: power of two up to 1024
Tap the number to enter a tempo, press +/−, or swipe up/down on the tempo number. TAP averages up to five intervals; after 2.5 seconds a new measurement starts.

The circular hand makes one revolution per BPM reference pulse; the pendulum reaches one turning point per pulse. The dot chain counts the time signature’s denominator beats. Tap the graphic to start or stop. Tap the dot chain to open Meter & beats: time signature, BPM reference, subdivision and swing under Meter & pulse; audible/muted beats and accents under Beats. Stopping resets to the beginning.

The BPM reference stays constant when the meter changes. Eighths and sixteenths are absolute note values. Swing shifts additional subdivisions only; main beats stay fixed. Muted main beats also suppress their subdivisions. 2:1 uses exactly two thirds. Markers show the actual events of the current reference pulse.

Tempo and reference change at the next pulse, sound and grid at the next bar, and meter and beat states together at the next bar boundary. Playback continues with the screen locked; audio interruptions stop it. The notification controls transport. Your last settings are saved automatically.
Reduced motion keeps the hand stationary. The light pulse remains visible. The pattern editor and training are not yet available.

Sounds: Standard click, Cut, Woodblock, Hi-hat, Snare and Cowbell. Tonal sounds can be tuned by ±12 semitones. Normal and accented hits change pitch together; duration and tempo stay unchanged. Preview plays accented, then normal. During playback changes take effect at the next bar.
Audio playback failed. Please try again.
Background playback could not be started. Please try again.

Tap the beat chain to edit patterns and training. Bars wrap into rows, with at most two per row. Tap a beat to cycle On → Accented → Off. Tap the remaining bar area to select it for duplication, moving or deletion. Only the gear opens its meter, subdivision and swing settings. The reference pulse applies to the whole pattern. Beat omissions protect the first count and its subdivisions, but do not restore deliberately muted beats. Whole-bar omissions also mute the first count. Tempo increases use playback time and take effect at the next bar. At the target, playback continues. Stop resets the run; changing tempo manually cancels automatic increases for this run. Save stores the default tempo separately from your current practice tempo.

Saving and loading show a short confirmation with the pattern name. The dumbbell in the main header indicates that omissions or tempo increases are enabled, including before playback starts. Tap it to open training settings. Each bar shows its subdivision and whether swing is active; swing requires a subdivision.

Bluetooth headphones can delay sound beyond the playback position reported by Android. If the picture is early, increase Picture delay in settings until the beat light and click agree. This shifts only the display, not the audio, and is a global manual setting: reset it when changing output devices. Bluetooth delay can vary, so exact synchronisation is not guaranteed. Playback always uses the short 40 ms preroll; audio routing adds further latency. TAP averages up to six taps (five intervals), restarting after a gap longer than 2.5 seconds. TAP sets tempo, not the beat phase of a song.
Long-short rhythm: dotted eighth and sixteenth
Long-short rhythm: dotted sixteenth and thirty-second
Time to target tempo: approx. %1$s min
